summary.oneLiner: Recently-IPO'd multi-fibre yarn maker (Silvassa anchor + new Punjab subsidiary) in a transition year: Punjab Phase-1 ramped to full only by end-Mar'26, so consol margins are temporarily depressed by depreciation/interest; FY27 should show steep operating-leverage recovery (EBITDA guided to ~2x) as Punjab stabilizes, technical-textile capacity doubles, and the value-added mix climbs.

thesis (one line): Recently-IPO'd multi-fibre yarn maker (Silvassa anchor + new Punjab subsidiary) in a transition year: Punjab Phase-1 ramped to full only by end-Mar'26, so consol margins are temporarily depressed by depreciation/interest; FY27 should show steep operating-leverage recovery (EBITDA guided to ~2x) as Punjab stabilizes, technical-textile capacity doubles, and the value-added mix climbs.
scorecard (q4 fy26):
**Consolidated (incl. Punjab subsidiary):**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 1,169.2 cr | +59.7% YoY, +8.4% QoQ | Punjab subsidiary now contributing |
| EBITDA | INR 94.4 cr | +38.1% YoY, +65% QoQ (vs INR 57.2 cr Q3) | margin 8.1% vs 5.3% Q3 FY26 |
| PAT (rptd) | INR 21.6 cr | — | depressed by Punjab depreciation + finance cost |

**Standalone (Silvassa):**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 752.8 cr | +3% (vs 731.2 cr) | full-capacity Silvassa |
| EBITDA | INR 82.5 cr | +16.9% (vs 70.6 cr) | margin 11% vs 9.7% Q4 FY25, 7% Q3 FY26 |
| PAT | INR 56.0 cr | +12.3% (vs 49.9 cr) | |

**FY26 full-year:** Consol rev INR 3,811.2 cr (+27.1% vs 2,996.6 cr); Consol EBITDA INR 284.4 cr (vs 263.5 cr); Consol PAT INR 77.3 cr. Standalone rev INR 3,037.9 cr (vs 2,996.8); Standalone EBITDA INR 277.1 cr (margin 9.1% vs 8.9%); Standalone PAT INR 191.9 cr (+10%).

**Volume:** Silvassa FY26 production 2.31 lakh MT, sales 2.28 lakh MT. **Value-added mix:** Silvassa >40% value-addition achieved; Punjab started at ~10%, intends to scale up.
**Net debt:** ~INR 1,325 cr (Mar'26 exit). **Gross debt:** ~INR 1,500 cr (peak); cost of debt ~7.25% (incl. PTA/MEG LC payables beyond 68 days).
**One-offs / non-recurring:** raw material in transit of ~INR 180 cr inflated inventory & sundry creditors; payable days rose 59→104 (mgmt says will normalize as full-quarter COGS base builds). Gas cost at Silvassa up ~50-60% (gas = ~6-7% of operational cost).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue FY27:** Silvassa ~INR 3,100 cr (vs ~3,000 FY26); Punjab ~INR 2,600 cr → **consol ~INR 5,600-5,700 cr**.
- **EBITDA FY27:** "north of INR 500 cr" (vs ~280 cr FY26) — i.e. nearly doubling; targets **double-digit consol EBITDA margin** (currently single digit; conservative given global situation). Tracks business on **EBITDA per ton** (if prices rise, % falls but per-ton holds).
- **PBT FY27:** ~INR 225-250 cr (after Punjab interest + depreciation; consol finance cost to stay north of INR 125 cr; depreciation run-rate ~INR 120 cr).
- **Capacity / capex:** Technical-yarn at Silvassa doubling 9,000 → 18,000 MTPA, commissioning **end of Q1 FY27 (July)**, adds ~INR 150 cr revenue. Punjab **Phase 2** targeted commission **end-FY28** (clarified, not FY27), takes Punjab to >INR 4,000 cr revenue. **Cotton expansion** in MP (Dhar, PM MITRA scheme): 50 acres bought (paid INR 26 cr), 72,000 spindles, possession by last quarter CY26, production ~10-12 months later → revenue from **H2 FY28**, adds INR 400-450 cr.
- **Peak revenue (by end-FY28):** ~INR 7,500-7,700 cr.
- **Debt repayment:** INR 100-125 cr payout/year; no big new debt planned; INR 1,500 cr is peak gross debt.
demand: Robust and recovering. Post-war volatility briefly disturbed downstream buyers but demand "back to base" and "very robust." Structural driver = consumer shift toward man-made / versatile fibres. Export sentiment improving (garments, home textiles) on easing tariffs and global sourcing diversification toward India. Cotton demand held up well despite sharp price escalation.
segment detail (polyester / cotton / tec:
- **Polyester filament yarn:** crude-linked; spreads good pre-war, compressed during war as RM (PTA/MEG) spiraled; pass-through stabilizing — "in process of passing on the entire hike." Mgmt cautiously constructive.
- **Cotton yarn:** significant uptick in yarn prices in Q4 on sharp spot raw-cotton rise + manufacturing-capacity disruption; margins up; FY27 raw-cotton availability a key watch (climate risk).
- **Technical/specialty yarn:** Silvassa capacity doubling; higher-value applications; growing focus area.
- No material polyester↔polyester-cotton blending shift expected from cotton price rise.
growth / optionality: Technical-textile doubling (Jul'26); Punjab Phase-2 (FY28, →INR 4,000 cr); MP cotton spindle expansion (50-acre PM MITRA plot with spare land for future). Possible forward integration / new growth leg — "concrete internal plans" hinted but not disclosed ("we will come back to you"). Exports ~5% of Silvassa volume; to rise on Silvassa but flat at consol level (Punjab serves North domestic).
margins & cost: Consol margin recovery driven by Punjab operating leverage / fixed-cost absorption as it ramps from 80-85% (Q1 FY27) toward Silvassa-like full utilization; product-mix realignment (eliminating low-fit products, adding value-added) completes through Q1 FY27 — full benefit visible from **Q2 FY27**. Solar: 32 MW hybrid solar from Serentica over 3 phases (Jul'26 → ~15 months), 3-year payback, benefit mainly FY28. Punjab uses agri-waste (no gas exposure); Silvassa gas cost up 50-60%.
capex: Punjab Phase-1 capitalized in FY26 (largest expansion in company history) — driving higher depreciation/finance cost this year. Phase-2 in works (orders to be announced), commission end-FY28. Technical-yarn doubling at Silvassa. MP cotton: INR 26 cr land + spindle capex (amount not disclosed). Solar via PPA (Serentica), not owned capex.
capital allocation (ipo proceeds): Disciplined: deleveraging INR 100-125 cr/yr; no large new debt; gross debt peaked at INR 1,500 cr. ECB in Euros fully hedged for loan tenure. Currency largely neutral (import-export natural balance + booking policy). Funding capacity expansion (Phase-2, technical, MP cotton) from internal accruals + measured debt.
risks:
- **Commodity:** crude-linked PTA/MEG volatility for polyester; pass-through lags in high volatility. Raw-cotton price/availability + climate risk for cotton. Gas cost up 50-60% at Silvassa.
- **PTA supply:** domestic GAIL & Indian Oil PTA plants delayed (GAIL paraxylene tied up by West Asia crisis → supply from Jul'26; IOC year-end) — domestic PTA price relief deferred to H2 FY27. PTA import-duty waiver status quo uncertain (could revert to 5%).
- **Demand / geopolitical:** West Asia war disrupted supply chains, spreads, downstream demand; "global environment fluid."
- **Chinese competition:** not explicitly raised; broader import-substitution / FTA tailwind is the offset.
- **Execution:** Punjab margin/value-add ramp dependent; working-capital normalization to be proven.
mgmt tone: Confident but deliberately conservative on margin %. Emphasizes EBITDA-per-ton over %; "rock solid" base operations during largest-ever expansion. Three FY27 pillars: operational stabilization & disciplined execution; improving demand/export environment; clear scalable growth road map. Repeatedly cautious on global/war situation.
non-obvious points:
- Punjab realization is at a small discount to standalone — but mgmt clarifies standalone blends in higher-priced cotton & technical yarn; pure filament gap is small (coarser North yarns + freight arbitrage deliberately shared with customers). NOT distress discounting.
- Mgmt does **not** track per-vertical (polyester/cotton/technical) P&L individually — no segment bifurcation given.
- Silvassa runs at ~95% (its optimal/"stressed" level) across all three yarns.
- Payable-days spike (59→104) is an artifact of partial-year Punjab COGS base + INR 180 cr RM-in-transit — expected to normalize, not a structural negative-WC improvement.
- Phase-2 timeline corrected mid-call from FY27 to FY28.
challenges → beneficiaries:
| Challenge / structural shift | Potential beneficiary |
|---|---|
| Man-made-fibre consumption shift + India-UK/EU FTAs + China+1 sourcing | Indian integrated yarn makers (Sanathan ✅) |
| Domestic PTA capacity (GAIL/IOC) coming on stream H2 FY27 | Polyester yarn spinners (RM cost relief) ⭐ |
| Cotton price spike + capacity disruption | Integrated cotton-yarn players with inventory discipline |

Standalone EBITDA margin 11% (vs 7% Q3). Punjab Phase-1 fully ramped only end-Mar'26 (a quarter late vs Dec target). Net debt ~INR 1,325 cr. FY27 guidance: rev INR 5,600-5,700 cr, EBITDA >INR 500 cr, double-digit margin target. Technical-yarn doubling commissions Jul'26; Punjab Phase-2 end-FY28; MP cotton H2 FY28. Peak rev ~INR 7,500-7,700 cr by end-FY28.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
